name: Victor Von Doom
comicBio: Latverian monarch, sorcerer and scientist — the rare Marvel villain who is a head of state first and a supervillain second.
His obsession begins with Reed Richards: a lab accident he blames on Reed scars his face and defines a lifetime of rivalry.
In Secret Wars (1984) he steals the Beyonder's power; in Jonathan Hickman's 2015 Secret Wars he becomes God Emperor Doom, stitching dead universes into Battleworld and ruling it as a god.
That Battleworld conceit — surviving fragments of collapsed realities fused into one patchwork world — is the comic spine Doomsday is built on.

name: Reed Richards
comicBio: The smartest man in his universe, transformed by cosmic rays on an unsanctioned space flight he talked his friends into taking.
Founder of the Illuminati in the comics — the secret council that meets whenever a threat is too big to admit publicly.
In Hickman's run it is Reed who first detects Incursions and builds the machines meant to stop two Earths from colliding.
His failure to save every universe is what hands the endgame to Doom.

name: Susan Storm
comicBio: The team's most powerful member and its emotional centre — the one who holds the family together when Reed disappears into a problem.
Her force fields scale from a bullet screen to a shield that can hold back a Celestial-tier assault.
In Secret Wars lore she is the moral counterweight to both Reed's calculation and Doom's tyranny.
As Franklin's mother she is directly tied to the most dangerous power in the multiverse.

name: Johnny Storm
comicBio: The hot-headed youngest of the four, able to ignite his entire body and fly at supersonic speeds.
His rivalry-turned-friendship with Ben Grimm is the longest-running double act in Marvel comics.
He has repeatedly wielded the Power Cosmic on loan, most famously when standing in for the Silver Surfer.
In cosmic arcs he is the F4 member most likely to end up on the wrong side of a Galactus negotiation.

name: Benjamin Grimm
comicBio: Test pilot and Reed's oldest friend, permanently transformed into an orange rock-skinned powerhouse.
The tragedy of the character is that he is the only one who cannot change back and pass as human.
In Battleworld-era stories his sheer durability makes him one of the few beings able to survive reality shearing.
His loyalty is the reason the family survives Doom over and over again.

name: Franklin Richards
comicBio: Son of Reed and Sue, and canonically one of the most powerful mutants ever born — an omega-level reality warper.
As a child he has created entire pocket universes, including one used to rebuild a destroyed Earth.
In Hickman's Secret Wars, Franklin and Molecule Man are literally the tools used to remake existence.
Any Doomsday endgame that restores a broken multiverse runs through a power source like his.

name: Galan of Taa
comicBio: The last survivor of the universe before ours, reborn as a cosmic force that consumes worlds to stay alive.
Not a villain so much as a natural law with a face — the Fantastic Four's defining antagonist since 1966.
His arrival always comes with a herald, and his hunger is what first proves Earth is worth defending on a cosmic scale.
In Incursion-era stories, world-eaters and world-collisions are two sides of the same extinction event.

name: Shalla-Bal
comicBio: A herald granted the Power Cosmic in exchange for leading Galactus to inhabited worlds.
The Surfer's defining story is the moment the herald refuses and turns on their master.
In the comics the herald's conscience is the first crack in Galactus's inevitability.
Heralds are also the multiverse's best scouts — the ones who see an Incursion coming.

name: Stephen Strange
comicBio: A surgeon whose ruined hands send him to Kamar-Taj, where he becomes Earth's foremost sorcerer.
As Sorcerer Supreme he is the multiverse's border guard — the one who knows what crossing over costs.
In the comics he is a founding member of the Illuminati and votes on the unthinkable when Incursions begin.
His willingness to break rules 'for the greater good' is exactly the flaw Doom exploits.

name: Peter Parker
comicBio: Bitten by a radioactive spider, driven by the single most quoted line in comics about power and responsibility.
The MCU's Peter is the youngest Avenger and the one with the least institutional protection.
Spider-Verse stories established that Spider-heroes exist in nearly every reality — and that some universes need theirs.
He is the emotional entry point for audiences into multiversal stakes.

name: Thor Odinson
comicBio: The Asgardian god of thunder, exiled to Earth to learn humility and never entirely successful at it.
One of the few Avengers whose lifespan is measured in millennia, giving him memory of older cosmic wars.
In Secret Wars-adjacent arcs, Thors serve as Battleworld's police force under God Emperor Doom.
That image — hammers deputised to a tyrant — is one of the sharpest visuals in the source material.

name: Sam Wilson
comicBio: A pararescue veteran who becomes the Falcon, then inherits the shield from Steve Rogers.
Unlike Steve, Sam carries the mantle without a super-soldier serum — the shield is a choice, not an upgrade.
Comic Sam repeatedly clashes with a government that wants Captain America to be an instrument of policy.
With no standing Avengers roster, he is the closest thing Earth has to a chairman when Doomsday hits.

name: James Buchanan Barnes
comicBio: Steve Rogers' oldest friend, presumed dead and rebuilt by HYDRA into a brainwashed assassin.
His arc is about earning an identity back from the people who programmed it out of him.
In the comics he has carried the shield himself and led black-ops teams as a Thunderbolt.
He now sits at the seam between the old Avengers and the government's new team.

name: Loki Laufeyson
comicBio: The God of Mischief, an adopted Frost Giant whose every scheme is really about being taken seriously.
His series turned him from the MCU's first villain into the load-bearing pillar of the timeline itself.
Comic Loki has died, been reborn as a child, and repeatedly chosen a better story over a written destiny.
Everything the audience knows about branching, pruning and Incursions was taught by his show.

name: Wanda Maximoff
comicBio: Sokovian volunteer turned reality-warper, powered by the Mind Stone and an innate gift for chaos magic.
House of M is her signature comic story: three words that rewrite mutantkind out of existence.
The Darkhold's promise — that a mother can reach across realities for her children — drives her darkest turn.
She proved Incursions are possible by walking between universes without a machine.

name: Scott Lang
comicBio: A thief with an engineering degree who inherits the Pym Particle suit and, with it, a second chance.
The Quantum Realm he travels through is the MCU's most reliable back door between realities.
It was Scott's rat-and-a-van accident that made the time heist — and the branched timelines — possible.
In the comics he is the everyman whose ordinary stakes make cosmic events legible.

name: Shaun / Shang-Chi
mcuDebut: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
comicBio: Raised as an assassin by his father and defined by the choice to walk away from that inheritance.
The Ten Rings are older than any Earth power on the board and their origin is still unexplained.
Comic Shang-Chi is Marvel's master of kung fu, unrivalled in unarmed combat even among enhanced beings.
The beacon his rings sent at the end of his film has never been answered on screen.

name: Clint Barton
comicBio: The Avenger with no powers, only an impossible aim and a very high tolerance for consequences.
His post-Blip story is about handing the bow to Kate Bishop and getting out alive.
Comic Clint has led the Thunderbolts and the West Coast Avengers, usually badly and always memorably.
He is the yardstick for what an unenhanced human is worth in a war over reality.

name: Bruce Banner
comicBio: A gamma physicist whose anger became a separate, indestructible person living in his body.
'Smart Hulk' merged the two, but the comics insist the truce is always temporary.
World War Hulk and Maestro show what he becomes when the restraints come off across timelines.
He also has a son, Skaar, waiting in the wings for the next global emergency.

name: Shuri
comicBio: Wakandan princess, engineering prodigy, and now the bearer of the Black Panther mantle.
Wakanda's vibranium reserves and tech make it a sovereign superpower, not a national ally.
Comic Shuri has held the mantle before and communes with the ancestral Djalia plane.
In a war over reality, Wakanda's science is one of the few Earth-side answers available.

name: Carol Danvers
comicBio: An Air Force pilot infused with Tesseract energy, making her the most powerful being on Earth's contact list.
She spends most of her time off-world managing the fallout of an empire she helped destabilise.
In the comics she has punched through dimensional barriers and survived unfiltered cosmic energy.
A hero who can travel between systems unaided is exactly who you send toward a collapsing universe.

name: Marc Spector
comicBio: A mercenary revived by the Egyptian god Khonshu, sharing his body with at least two other identities.
His stories are Marvel's most direct exploration of dissociative identity as both wound and weapon.
Because his power comes from a god outside the usual cosmology, he answers to no Earth authority.
The moment reality frays, unaligned assets like Marc get pulled in whether they consent or not.

name: Matt Murdock
comicBio: Blinded as a child by radioactive chemicals that hyper-charged every remaining sense.
Lawyer by day, vigilante by night — Marvel's most explicitly Catholic hero and its most guilt-driven.
Born Again is the comic benchmark for stripping a hero down to nothing and rebuilding him.
When the sky opens, someone has to be holding the block-level line in New York.

name: Vision
comicBio: A synthezoid built from Ultron's body, JARVIS's mind and the Mind Stone's power.
White Vision, reactivated without memory or emotion, is still unaccounted for.
Comic Vision's arc is a machine repeatedly asking whether it is allowed to be a person.
A synthetic Avenger with density control is one of the few beings who can survive a phase-shifted reality.

name: Wong
comicBio: Master of the mystic arts, librarian of Kamar-Taj and current holder of the Sorcerer Supreme title.
The MCU's most consistently competent adult in a room full of reckless geniuses.
Comic Wong is the anchor who keeps the Sanctums standing when Strange oversteps.
Sanctum security is literally multiverse border control.

name: Eric Brooks
comicBio: A dhampir — born with vampire strengths and none of the weaknesses — who hunts his own kind.
Wesley Snipes' 1998 film is the reason the modern superhero movie exists at all.
Comic Blade operates outside every superhuman registry, which makes him useful and unaccountable.
Supernatural threats scale badly during reality collapse, and Blade is Earth's specialist.

name: Valentina Allegra de Fontaine
mcuDebut: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)
comicBio: A CIA power broker quietly assembling deniable operatives across half a dozen MCU projects.
In the comics Val is revealed as Madame Hydra — the ally you should never have briefed.
She is the reason the government has a superhero team on retainer and the Avengers do not.
Whoever controls the branding when Doomsday starts controls the public's version of events.

name: Yelena Belova
comicBio: A Red Room graduate freed from chemical conditioning, and Natasha's chosen sister.
Comic Yelena has worn the Widow name as rival, successor and occasional villain.
She is the reluctant centre of the government's new team — the one with a conscience and a body count.
Her arc asks whether a weapon can choose what it is pointed at.

name: Robert Reynolds
comicBio: The power of a million exploding suns, wrapped around a man with severe mental illness.
Every Sentry story is really about the Void — the destroyer that shares his mind and undoes his good.
In the comics he is the single most powerful being the Avengers have ever had on the roster, and the most dangerous.
Against a universe-level threat, Sentry is the only Earth-side asset in the correct weight class.

name: Alexei Shostakov
comicBio: The Soviet Union's answer to Captain America, decades past his prime and still telling the stories.
Comic Alexei was Natasha's husband before the state erased the marriage from both their records.
He is the team's comic relief and its most sincere believer in the idea of being a hero.
In a lineup of assets, he is the one who wants a family more than a mission.

name: John Walker
mcuDebut: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)
comicBio: A decorated soldier handed the shield by a government that wanted a more obedient Captain America.
Comic Walker is the cautionary version of the ideal: same serum, no restraint, state supervision.
Stripped of the title, he becomes the enforcer Val keeps on a very short leash.
He embodies what happens when a symbol is nationalised.

name: Antonia Dreykov
comicBio: Photographic reflexes: she reproduces any fighting style after seeing it once.
Comic Taskmaster is a mercenary instructor who trains the henchmen of half the Marvel villain roster.
The trade-off is memory — every skill learned pushes a piece of her own life out.
A fighter who can copy an Avenger's technique is a cheap counter to almost any hero.

name: Ava Starr
comicBio: A quantum accident left her permanently phasing between states, in constant pain and out of sync with reality.
Comic Ghost is a corporate saboteur; the MCU rewrote her as a victim of the same science that made Ant-Man.
Her phasing is quantum-realm adjacent, which makes her useful where physics is already failing.
She is the team member most literally caught between two realities.

name: James Howlett / Logan
comicBio: A mutant with a healing factor, heightened senses and a skeleton laced with adamantium by the Weapon X programme.
Two centuries of memory, most of it taken from him and slowly recovered.
In Secret Wars' Battleworld, Old Man Logan crosses from a ruined timeline into the patchwork world and refuses to accept it as real.
That exact move — a legacy variant walking into a stitched-together reality — is the Doomsday playbook.

name: Wade Wilson
comicBio: A terminal cancer patient given a corrupted healing factor that keeps him alive and disfigured.
The only Marvel character who knows he is in a comic and negotiates with the reader about it.
Comic Deadpool has killed the Marvel Universe, joined X-Force, and been trusted with far too much cosmic hardware.
He is the audience's translator for the rules of anchor beings, the Void and TVA salvage.

name: Charles Xavier
mcuDebut: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
comicBio: The world's most powerful telepath and founder of the school that gives mutants somewhere to be children.
Cerebro extends his mind across a planet — and, in some stories, across realities.
He is a founding Illuminati member: the man who erases memories when the council votes to hide something.
His Earth-838 appearance is proof that multiple Xaviers exist and can be summoned.

name: Erik Lehnsherr
comicBio: Holocaust survivor turned master of magnetism, convinced that coexistence is a story humans tell before the camps.
The most persuasive villain in Marvel comics precisely because his history keeps proving him partly right.
In Secret Wars-era stories he has ruled, protected and abandoned mutantkind by turns.
Any incoming X-Men era needs its Erik, and two actors have already played him.

name: Scott Summers
comicBio: Field leader of the X-Men, firing uncontrollable optic force beams behind a ruby-quartz visor.
His discipline is the reason the team functions and the reason nobody likes him at first.
Comic Scott eventually leads a mutant revolution, becoming the movement's most divisive figure.
Legacy-timeline X-Men are prime candidates for salvage when their universe destabilises.

name: Jean Grey
comicBio: Omega-level telepath and telekinetic, bonded with the cosmic Phoenix Force.
The Dark Phoenix Saga is the genre's original 'hero becomes extinction event' story.
The Phoenix operates above individual universes, making Jean one of few mutants with multiversal reach.
Reality-warpers of her class are exactly who gets drafted when the walls come down.

name: Hank McCoy
comicBio: A brilliant geneticist whose own experiments turned him blue, furred and superhumanly agile.
The X-Men's scientist, diplomat and the one most likely to break the timeline trying to fix it.
Comic Hank has pulled the original five X-Men out of the past — a canonical timeline violation.
A Beast variant has already surfaced in the 616's neighbourhood.

name: Remy LeBeau
comicBio: A Louisiana thief who charges objects with kinetic energy — most famously a deck of cards.
Raised by the Thieves Guild, permanently untrustworthy and permanently forgiven.
Comic Remy has served both the X-Men and Mister Sinister, which makes his loyalty an open question.
He is one of the Void's stranded survivors, already proven salvageable across realities.

name: Clea Strange
mcuDebut: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
comicBio: Ruler of the Dark Dimension and Dormammu's niece, raised inside a reality with different physics.
In the comics she is Strange's wife and eventually Sorcerer Supreme in her own right.
She specialises in the exact problem the MCU now has: repairing an Incursion.
Her arrival is a plot device with a scalpel — she came to fix something Strange broke.

name: America Chavez
mcuDebut: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
comicBio: Born in a pocket universe, able to punch star-shaped holes between realities.
The only character in the MCU with native, unassisted multiversal travel.
Comic America is a founding Young Avenger and one of Marvel's most prominent Latina heroes.
Her power is the single most strategically valuable asset in a war fought across universes.

name: Monica Rambeau
comicBio: S.W.O.R.D. agent transformed by passing through Wanda's Hex, able to convert her body into any energy on the spectrum.
Comic Monica led the Avengers under the Captain Marvel name long before Carol did.
Her powers make her a walking sensor array for electromagnetic and dimensional anomalies.
She ended her last appearance on the wrong side of a reality — and someone there recognised her.

name: Namor McKenzie
comicBio: King of an undersea civilisation and, in the comics, Marvel's very first mutant.
Founding Illuminati member — and the one who advocates destroying other Earths to save his own.
In Hickman's Incursion arc he does exactly that, forming the Cabal when the others hesitate.
No character is more directly tied to the moral logic of an Incursion than Namor.
